title: (Tinker) Surveillance
description_plain:
You can create devices and programs designed to gather information on specific targets. This ranges from software that can reconstruct every action taken on a specific computer going back to the time it was built, cameras that can pick out and track every person in a crowd at the highest resolution and see objects hidden on or even inside their person, directional microphones that can catch and separate every single voice in a crowded train-station or translate minuscule vibrations of a windowpane into all noise produced in the room, from music to conversation, etc.

This also includes the ability to disguise your creations to make them less likely to be noticed, whether that is by making the microphone the size of a small ant, or disguising your array of vibration-sensors that keeps track of every person in a football-stadium as bin holders with actual bins attached. However your aptitude is inferior to that of (Tinker) Camouflage, and an experienced observer knowing roughly where to look will discover your technology given a bit of time.

Your technology is exceptional at what it does, but it is stationary and has no direct offensive or defensive capabilities in and of itself, though it synergizes very well with other Tinker-Powers.

title: (Tinker/Thinker) One Man’s Trash Is Another Man’s Treasure
description_plain:
You can create advanced technology from the discarded remnants of society. What others see as trash, you see as the raw materials for innovation. From broken appliances, rusted metal, shattered glass, and forgotten scraps, you can craft advanced tinkertech from.

The more unwanted and neglected the materials, the more potent the technology you can create. A crumpled soda can becomes the casing for a powerful energy core, while a pile of twisted wires can be reassembled into a neural interface that surpasses cutting-edge designs. Your ability’s main focus lies in this inversion of value—the deeper the rejection and abandonment of the materials, the more powerful and advanced your creations become. This doesn’t necessarily mean the material has to be low quality, just that it has been “thrown away”. This specialty allows you to boost any other tinker power you have as long as you use trash to build.

You can sense just how unwanted an item is, when you encounter a discarded object, you instinctively know how much it’s been overlooked, forgotten, or discarded, and this perception fuels your creativity. Rummaging through trash and sifting through the most disgusting refuse poses no problem for you; in fact, you see it as a treasure hunt. Where others see filth and decay, you see potential and untapped energy, and you’re unfazed by the dirt and grime. The more unwanted an object, the more your excitement grows.

title: (Tinker) Ruggedization
description_plain:
You specialize in material reinforcement, employing methods such as specialized coatings, dipping, doping, or additive integration to fundamentally alter the properties of any base material.

With a single application, you can render metal immune to rust, make asphalt and concrete crackproof for centuries, and turn wood, plastic, or glass into weatherproof, shatter-resistant composites; you can also make advanced composite materials, such as variable-resistance semiconductors, near-perfect insulators of all types, pressure-sensitive foams, and custom lenses for a variety of purposes.

Furthermore, your ability dramatically improves the efficiency of mechanical systems by reducing friction and wear in moving parts, gears, and engines, enabling machinery to operate with near-frictionless precision and minimal maintenance.

This power works best when paired with other Tinker powers, but especially well with (Tinker) Chemistry.

title: (Tinker) Overclock
description_plain:
You specialize in pushing technology beyond its breaking point. Normally, your inventions appear modest or even underwhelming, but under high-pressure conditions or intense need, you can rapidly amplify their capabilities to extraordinary and destructive levels. Components hum, glow, and vibrate on the brink of self-destruction as your inventions deliver overwhelming performance—turning ordinary tools into engines of chaos.

While overclocking grants immense power, your equipment deteriorates as quickly as it gains strength, risking catastrophic meltdown and leaving behind molten wreckage and scorched battlefields.

This power works best when paired with other Tinker powers, but especially well with (Tinker) Repair, (Tinker) Salvage and (Tinker) Ruggedization.

title: (Tinker) Necromancer
description_plain:
You specialize in Tinker technology centered around corpses and dead biological matter, enabling you to work with any suitably "dead" carbon-based organism, whether animal, plant or... human.

This specialisation allows you to reanimate corpses through various techniques. You can create puppet-like skeletons reinforced with mechanical frameworks, inject chemical agents to reactivate a corpse's biosystems or repair and replicate dead cells via specialised nanites.

You can produce a variety of "undead", from stereotypical zombies and skeletons to Frankensteinian monstrosities and vampire-like beings. You can build numerous enhancements into these corpses, making them far more powerful in death than in life, and combine bodies to form horrifying hybrids.

Your expertise extends beyond reanimation, covering post-mortem brain data extraction, grafting dead limbs to the living and numerous other corpse-based technologies. However, you’re limited by material condition: the more decomposed the tissue is, the less viable it becomes, with excessive decay rendering it useless. Any parahumans you reanimate retain their powers if their Corona Pollentia remains intact.

title: (Tinker) Rapid Prototyping
description_plain:
You specialize in producing limited proof-of-concepts for more ambitious tinker projects, at a fraction of the time and cost. This only works if you already have a solid idea of what you're working towards. That idea has to be within your capacity to implement, given enough time, though one of the benefits of this specialty is that data the inferior version generates can be used to improve its inevitable replacement. This is especially true if the device is used in a wide variety of situations, or if it's pushed to it's limits in more extreme ways, such as combat.

From ray-guns that can't be reloaded once fired, to teleporters with long charge-ups and limited range, it's up to you to decide what corners exactly get cut (and by how much). Be careful about letting durability suffer too dramatically: once you're ready to upgrade to a superior version, you'll find that cannibalizing prototypes can save you a lot of labor, if they're reasonably intact. If they're well-tested in addition, this could entirely make up for the time put into their original construction.

You won't find much benefit from this if you can spend all week in your workshop assembling your megaproject. But if you've got stuff to do, you can rest assured that your long-term ambitions won't suffer for the time lost, as long as you break your work up into prototypes and don't wait too long between upgrades.

This power gives you access to a wide-but-shallow repository of generic supertech, but it truly shines when combined with other tinker specialties. It pairs especially well with specialties that trade high time or resource costs for increased effectiveness, like (Tinker) Electromagnetism or (Tinker/Trump) Power Tinker, ensuring that you have something functional to show for your work during the large ramp-up times that those specialties demand.

title: (Tinker) Clockwork Precision
description_plain:
Your Tinker specialization lies in Synchronicity: technology that works best when used/activated in concert with the occurrence of a predefined event. i.e. a shield that blocks attacks better if you’ve just provoked your attacker to speak; a set of mortars that work best when fired in sync or canon with each other to increase the spread of the destruction or maximize damage to the bombarded area; a crossbow that pierces through solid slabs of concrete when it's knocked and fired to an inbuilt beat, but is little better than a BB gun if operated too far off beat.

The efficacy of the tinkertech inversely scales to the controllability and commonality of the event it's synchronised to; becoming better the harder it is to time the use of the tinkertech to the event it's built for.

On its own, this Tinker specialization doesn't work well with electricity, instead being clockwork themed.

title: (Tinker) Precision
description_plain:

Tolerances and margins of error are for others; you aim for perfection—down to the finest detail. Every gear meshes flawlessly, every circuit is calibrated to perfection, and every tool is built to perform at its peak, every time, with zero tolerance for errors.

Your creations accomplish feats of engineering accuracy that defy reason: your automated turrets hit bullseyes through dozens of ricochets, your chemical stations synthesize compounds or solutions exact down to the molecule, and your mechanical limbs are steady enough to paint the Mona Lisa on an electron cloud. However, this comes at a cost—your Tinkertech requires more time, resources and maintenance compared to most other Tinkers.

Your devices might lack raw firepower, but their efficiency, precision, and consistency make them the best choice for any situation that requires discretion.

This pairs exceedingly well with most other Tinker powers.

title: (Tinker) Filter
description_plain:
You can manufacture circular filtering portals that separate things from other things and redirect them away. The portals themselves have no true physical existence, as they are simple two-dimensional spatial anomalies. Each portal is surrounded by a ring of machinery that is responsible for the creation and stability of the spatial portal. The portals can be any size, as long as they are completely contained within stabilizing machinery. For the same reason, moving a portal's location can be an ordeal.

The filtering for these portals can work with selectable specificity, meaning you can remove above or under a limit, singular types or a spectrum, matter and energies both. Metals from ore, UV-rays from sunlight, pollution from water, all can be removed, redirected and contained. Only the smaller portion can be transported away to a specific receptacle attached to the portal.

The portals work in two directions, removing things while the flow through them is one way, and adding things back from the input/output receptacle when the flow moves to the other direction. Either way, the flow becomes homogenous, as the portals equalize any incoming variance in their output.

Warning: as living beings normally can not survive being homogenized, travel through the portal is not recommended.

title: (Tinker) Electromagnetism
description_plain:
You specialize in the manipulation of electromagnetic fields, waves and currents. Your specialization is incredibly broad, allowing you to construct railguns, arc throwers, personal magnetic forcefields, mag-lev flight systems, electromagnetic lockpicks, and multispectral visors that allow you to see through walls via radio frequencies.

However, your creations are power hungry, and your specialization does not exactly include convenient ways of generating power, forcing you to siphon power off of the existing power grid via induction, or to carry oversized chemical batteries with you. Furthermore, your technology also has high material standards - a gadget made with high purity metals will both be much more powerful and last significantly longer than one made with scavenged copper or impure alloys.

All of this makes you a "Win-More" tinker: nearly unstoppable given a secure, well-funded workshop and access to the power grid, but forced into desperate, self-destructive tactics when cut off from civilization.

title: (Tinker) Resource Exploitation
description_plain:
This power grants a Tinker specialty revolving around resource gathering. Which might sound a bit boring but in practice means that once you have a half way decent setup you’ll never have to worry about resource shortages other Tinkers might suffer, at least when it comes to resources that can be found in regions you can harvest resources from.

The technology offered by this power offers a versatile array of options towards harvesting resources in various environments. But the focus for that harvesting is through the use of personal equipment, the kind a miner might use in a sci-fi setting.

So you can make things like handheld mining lasers that separate desired materials from what they’re pointed at and teleport them up to thousands of meters away into a connected container, or a water filtration system able to ensure pure drinking water from even the most polluted sources.

Another example could be making power armor, with advanced sensors capable of locating desired materials through hundreds of meters of earth and moving hundreds of tons of useless rock out of the way.

Of course like other Tinkers you can experiment to make technology that diverges from your specialty especially for combat such as the construction of weapons and armor.

However, given that this power touches little on combat, the idiosyncrasies of its specialty will be apparent in such Tinkertech, for good and ill.

An example of this could be that power armor you could build being able to easily support and move hundreds of tons making carrying heavy weaponry or feats of raw brute strength easy, but be relatively frail compared to the power armor of a combat focused Tinker who has a similar level of resources and development to you.

A second example could be those laser tools you make could be designed to ignore organic matter, making them perfect for disabling the equipment of any opponent, but as it was based off a mining tool it is relatively short range with a massive drop off in effectiveness beyond a few feet.

title: (Tinker) Home on the Road
description_plain:
You specialize in mobile homes and RVs, the chosen vehicle of people who can’t afford an actual home (you) and the rich. Trailers and caravans that can be pulled by nearly any vehicle and placed just about anywhere, motorhomes for that genuine home-on-the-road feel, campers for those who want to sleep under the stars for a week but just can’t leave home behind, the whole shebang is yours to design and create.

You have a knack for interior design when it comes to homes in general, but especially those built into vehicles. title: (Tinker) Dream Craft
description_plain:
While awake you only have normal access to your Tinker powers. But if you happen to sleep in your lab or even just around adequate supplies, you will dream.

Except for the fact you will be guaranteed to have them in those scenarios these will be regular dreams. The catch however is that during those dreams your body will begin to sleepwalk and build a random piece of Tinker-tech based around the dreams you were having. This Tinker-tech will be far more advanced and powerful compared to your waking efforts.

As an example, if you have Tinker powers centered on enhancing the physical capabilities of living beings but normally your best work can only compare to the average Brute, then a dream about eating food can lead your sleeping self to make a candy that when eaten temporarily grants a Brute rating of 10. Which for context is comparable to Behemoth.

You are perfectly capable of maintaining, repairing, and even modifying technology you built while asleep so long as it isn’t destroyed beyond repair. However the more you modify that technology away from the design you made while asleep the simpler and weaker it will become until it’s just like the tinkertech you can make while awake.

Synergy with other Tinker powers is possible, but mostly revolving around integrating the technology you can make into martial arts.

title: (Tinker) Hyperspecialized
description_plain:
You have the power to improve one aspect of tinkertech, whether it be the durability, functionality, or utility, to an incredible degree, but this will come at a price, with every other aspect of the piece degrading to almost unusable levels. With this power, you can create hyper-specialized technology, able to do one thing to a level of mastery, but falling short when trying to perform any other function.

Whether it's building a machine that can lift a hundred tons but breaks at a gust of wind, or building a computer that can process a million times more data per second than the current supercomputers but has no memory to store the data, you have the ability to create machines that can exceed anything ever created before, with one caveat: they have to excel at only one thing at the cost of failing at everything else.

title: (Tinker) Chassis
description_plain:
You can create many types of basic devices, such as vehicles, robots, or weapons. These devices are somewhat larger than usual, while having very unremarkable capabilities for tinkertech. However, they have slots that other tinkertech can be inserted, after which they will reconfigure and transform to gain capabilities based on the inserted tinkertech.

For example, a plasma rifle made by you can take an electro-tinker’s tesla coil and gain the ability to shoot a 500 Gigawatt beam. You could put a tinkertech diving suit into a truck to cause it to transform into an amphibious submersible. Placing a biotinker’s med-scanner into a supercomputer would install programs that could track health and sickness in an entire city.

By default, this does not allow you to create tinkertech that can be slotted in, unless you have other Tinker specializations, especially broad modular ones like (Tinker) Add-On Augmentation and (Tinker) Basic Tinker

title: (Tinker) Murder
description_plain:
Your tinker speciality is a grim and purposeful art: the creation of killing machines.

You construct overly complex and overbuilt killing machines using primitive, outdated technology and the poorest quality materials available. Each device is a single-purpose instrument, engineered not just to kill, but to kill in a specific, often theatrical, manner. Instead of guns, you build guillotines. Instead of traps, you build iron maidens and pendulum blades.

Your focus is on categorizing and inflicting distinct forms of death. One device may be designed solely for precise beheading, another for systematic exsanguination, and another for slow compression or piercing. Your technology favors direct, physical intervention over energy weapons or subtlety, relying on gears, counterweights, rusty iron, and sharpened steel. As long as it was made to kill in particular gruesome ways and doesn’t used overly advanced technology, anything can be build, from automatons to vehicles.

Despite its crude and brutalist construction, the sheer mechanical redundancy and over-engineering render your devices unnaturally robust and potent, allowing a massive spring-powered spear launcher to match the range and piercing power of a fellow Tinker's railgun, or a clockwork automaton to grapple with a powered armor suit. However, this comes at the cost of any practicality; your creations are labyrinthine tangles of levers, exposed mechanisms, and idiosyncratic controls, making them hopelessly unwieldy and dangerously unpredictable for anyone but you to operate.

The archaic technology and shoddy materials demand constant, grueling maintenance, more so than other tinkertech. Due to its overbuilt design, such maintenance is near impossible as well. Luckily, through function, your tinkertech can maintain and even make lesser repairs itself. A blade being used to behead will not dull, a gear train that drives a crushing press will not wear, and rust will not spread so long as the device is periodically used to fulfill its lethal purpose, no matter if it’s not cleaned. The act of killing cleanses, sharpens, and repairs your tinkertech. This doesn’t improve your tech in any way, merely fulfils the act of maintenance.

title: (Tinker) Workout
description_plain:
Your tinker specialization is, in a somewhat broad sense: technology able to increase a person's capabilities. This technology, on a more mundane level, can indeed include gym equipment, weights, etc. In fact, you can go to your local gym and augment any equipment yourself.

But on the higher end, you could have weighted clothing that weighs upward of a few hundred kilos, exercise equipment that detect the users bio-signs and adapt to make the workout harder, and even certain drugs that can temporarily stop your physical growth in exchange for an even greater strength boost once its effects "wear off." Your average joe could go from being able to bench press 200 pounds, to being confused for a lower end Brute and Mover even if they don't have superpowers.

However, when it comes to powers, it isn't nearly as fast as (Tinker) Amplifiers and Dampeners, since this focuses more on the physical.

This works very well with other Tinker specialties, like (Tinker) Density, (Tinker) Amplifiers and Dampeners, and (Tinker) Refinement.

description_plain:
You're a Tinker specialized in working and living underground.

You can create both personal mining equipment and larger boring machines. From lightweight exoskeletons equipped with rock splitters, to massive drilling rigs, you can produce machines which dig through the earth with ease.

Digging randomly underground is dangerous. Luckily, you can make devices that scan and map the depths. This includes ground-penetrating radar systems and advanced surveying equipment, revealing objects, materials, and structures hidden beneath the surface.

To facilitate long-term subterranean survival, you're able to construct some buildings. For instance, you could build compact hydroponic or mushroom farms, oxygen scrubbers and support structures.

title: (Tinker) Avatar
description_plain:
You specialize in the creation of bodies that you can remotely control, transfer consciousness into either permanently or temporarily, or introduce a copy of the original consciousness into. Such bodies can be made from virtually anything.

They can be perfect clones of yourself or any individual and controlled accordingly. Or you can create an android built in such a way that it is difficult to distinguish from a human being. You could even interact with a virtual/cybernetic worlds if they exist, creating a virtual body capable of navigating and interacting with them. It can be any body you wish to inhabit.

Your specialty comes with a broad range of highly generalized technological trees, enough to allow you to make any type of modification you desire to the bodies you create, both in appearance and in the capabilities you can grant them. However, you will never surpass highly specialized fields such as (Tinker) Communication or any specialty you attempt to compete with directly.

Keep in mind that you are only capable of controlling one body at a time, and the same applies to anyone who wishes to transfer themselves into another body. Unless you possess multitasking capabilities or some special condition that allows you to generate a hive mind. A good measure to overcome this limitation would be to grant them AI, though whether they are loyal or not would depend on their programming.

You cannot apply this specialty to yourself or others only to the bodies you create. If you chose Shardless, your bodies will be able to house your powers.

description_plain: You can create advanced guns, though nothing that can't be transported by a non-Brute person. You'd also have to know where the core was, and the Endbringer might be able to dodge it even if you aimed correctly.

You can create a worldwide seismic wave emitter inducing localized quakes and faults, as well as a seismic wave dampener to promptly mitigate them. Essentially, you can create anything involving the Earth’s structure and all that is tangentially related to a lesser degree. This can trump Behemoth’s volcanic eruptions.

Additionally, you have an innate sense of style and design, allowing you to instinctively craft technology that is stylish. This makes it so that everything you create is exclusively good-looking, making even the most utilitarian gadgets visually striking.

This pairs well with other Tinker powers.

description_plain:
You specialize in the creation of tinkertech centered around the concept of 'toys'. You can construct a wide range of tinkertech oriented around this theme; miniature action figures that can move and fight, weaponised bladed yo-yos, huge toy robots able to fight Brutes, toy guns with lethal effects, explosive marble grenades, remote-controlled toy drones, decryption devices in the style of a Rubik's Cube and more.

From implementing existing technology into toys to improving toy designs to be unbelievably efficient and effective, there are few limits to what you can build under this theme. This pairs very well with (Tinker) Electronics and (Tinker) Mechanics.

title: (Tinker) Bonsai
description_plain:
You have a tinker specialization in the creation and manipulation of “technological seeds”. These seeds do nothing initially, but they will mutate over time to become various pieces of technology, gaining random modifiers to their existing functions or even entirely new features (their very first mutation will always be gaining some kind of feature, which will influence the chances of all future mutations).

Your tinker specialization gives you the tools to manipulate the growth of your seeds, including speeding up the rate of mutation; encouraging and discouraging them to/from certain types of mutations; and pruning away any unwanted mutations that have occurred (although you cannot choose to keep only part of a mutation, so if a mutation manifested as a positive & a negative, you would be removing the positive alongside the negative if you chose to remove it).

With sufficient time, resources, and the right string of mutations, you could hypothetically grow tinkertech from any tinkers tech tree as effectively as the tinkers themselves.

This synergizes well with other Tinker powers, as they will give you the ability to heavily influence the mutations in the direction of your other specializations, allowing you to produce tech for those trees cheaper than building them directly, although at the cost of potentially having to spend a long time pruning mutations to get the fine details you may desire.

title: (Tinker) Infusionist
description_plain:
You know that sci-fi trope of describing something as energy-infused to say it’s stronger and more capable than it normally would be? Yeah, this Tinker specialty revolves around that concept.

You can create items—handheld consumables—that infuse strange types of energy into whatever you desire.

These energy infusions are usually temporary buffs that can do things like increase structural integrity and defense, impart heat, kinetic energy, electricity, repair damage, etc. The sky’s the limit as all sorts of useful buffs are at your disposal.

For a few examples, the average energy infusion will last around a minute while being capable of increasing the defensive capabilities of a modern tank tenfold, or being capable of enhancing an iron sword to cut through bank vaults like warm butter, and that’s before you consider any strange or esoteric capabilities you added to the energy infusion.

But you aren’t limited to just temporary enhancements; you can create generators that can be integrated into items and will continuously release a desired type of energy into them so long as it has power.

Finally, this specialty grants a minor focus of its techbase on metallurgy and general engineering, so you can create personal equipment such as weapons and armor to infuse.

You are a wide-reaching tinker whose specialization revolves entirely around backpacks. Anything you create or design must be capable of fitting inside a backpack and supporting its weight in such a way that the user can carry and operate it without issue. This restriction applies across all types and sizes of backpacks.

This can range from a functional, controllable jetpack that allows you to fly, to a backpack from which multiple tentacles emerge, ending in human-like hands or equipped tools designed for multitasking.

title: (Tinker/Master) Spawners
description_plain:
You build compact, palm-sized spawner devices that are easy to fuel using ambient energy sources like solar, thermal, or kinetic input, making them highly energy-efficient during operation. They require regular hands-on maintenance to prevent drift and component degradation, as with any tinkertech, but their low power draw means a single device can run for weeks between refuels under normal conditions.

When activated, a spawner saturates a designated area with a non-reactive energy that poses no danger to ambient matter or people, and its range scales upward based on how much fuel you supply. This energy within that saturated area automatically coalesces and stabilises into solid entities without further input from you. You can choose to concentrate the energy into fewer, stronger entities or spread it thinly for larger numbers of weaker ones, at your discretion.

The resulting entities follow a detailed but script-like behavioral program that can be mistaken for animal intelligence, lacking true adaptability or learning, though the script can be extensive enough to mimic basic threat assessment and patrolling. When an entity dies inside its spawn area, its form disperses safely and returns to the ambient energy field, reforming after a cooldown of at least one hour that increases with the entity's strength, with no maximum upper limit. Death outside the spawn area causes permanent destruction with no respawn, taking longer to replace.

Before spawning, you set each entity's form, abilities, and behaviors via the device's controls, but you have no influence over them after they spawn unless you specifically built a loyalty protocol into that preset script. You can place multiple spawners in the same area to produce different creature types simultaneously.

title: (Tinker/Trump) Kryptonite
description_plain:
You build devices that emit a directed, short-range radiation harmless to ordinary humans but debilitating to certain parahumans, with each device calibrated during construction to exploit specific vulnerabilities in how a target's power operates at a fundamental physics level.

When building a device, you select three targeting parameters: function (the underlying mechanism, like dimensional folding or quantum locking), appearance (the observable expression, such as Alexandria packages or pyrokinesis), and match purity (how exclusively the target's power aligns with your first two choices; a pure match suffers full drain, while additional unrelated abilities reduce effectiveness). For example, you build a device set to the function to gravity manipulation and its appearance to Alexandria package. A target whose power is purely an Alexandria package driven by gravity manipulation suffers full drain. However, a cape who also flies via gravity manipulation but additionally has laser eyes (different appearance) automatically matches less on purity, so the radiation weakens. Similarly, a cape who flies via telekinesis (different function) despite looking like an Alexandria package also cases the radiation to weaken.

The radiation manifests as a colored glow unique to the target type, and within its limited range it saps strength, coordination, and power reliability, but disperses harmlessly beyond that range.

Improving your power expands the device's effective radius and allows broader targeting parameters. For example, a wide targeting like “all Brutes” requires a larger, hungrier device and delivers weaker radiation than a narrow “gravity-manipulating Strikers with no flight.”

Now, every device you create has its own unique mode, but all of them are inherently compatible with each other, allowing them to connect, fuse, and integrate to form new hybrid devices.

Each piece of technology you build follows the same core principles as before—every device has a specific mode it can shift into, like a gun that transforms into a scythe or a shield that expands into a giant fan. However, now these devices can merge while in their active modes, creating entirely new constructs with combined capabilities. title: (Tinker/Thinker) Legacy
description_plain:
You have the touch-based ability to learn the lore of objects, giving you an understanding of the age and various things achieved using them. This includes snippets of information about their previous users where the object in question is concerned.

You are a Tinker, specialized in using "artifacts" to produce thematically related devices. You are capable of breaking down existing objects into Tinkertech with functionality based on their past uses. The effects produced are influenced by the purposes the item was used for and the philosophy of its past wielders (e.g., you produce dramatically different things using the weapon of a pacifist compared to the weapon of a bloodthirsty warmonger).

The more significant and grander the accomplishments of the item, the more powerful the ensuing Tinkertech will be. A freshly made knife wouldn't be usable at all, but a knife used by an effectively powerless mortal to slay a god-like being against all odds could be easily and cheaply turned into an S-class superweapon.

title: (Tinker) Basic Tinker
description_plain:
This power grants access to an expansive, if somewhat generalized and basic, tinkertech base to build with. In other words, you can build any sci-fi technological or biological phenomena you can think of, as long as they are on the low end of sci-fi strength.

So while versatile, you’re never going to be able to overcome the average Tinker in their own specialty. You can, however, match the average Tinker’s casual efforts in their specialty.

To put this into perspective, a power armor Tinker might be able to build power armor that can withstand blows from an Endbringer, while you’ll struggle just to make power armor that has defensive capabilities similar to a modern tank. Another example could be a laser Tinker being able to build a handheld laser weapon that can pierce through over a dozen meters of steel, while your handheld laser weapons might take a few shots to destroy a tank.

It’s not all bad, though; you can stack multiple different types of technology in your favor to compensate for their individual weaknesses. Using a combination of power armor, forcefields, cybernetics, and bio-enhancements to provide you with a respectable level of defense, for example.

title: (Tinker) Russian Roulette
description_plain:
You are a Free Tinker, able to build practically any tinkertech permitted within an Entities' cycle that you can think of. However, you are restricted in that all of your tinkertech is reliant on the luck of the draw to work.

When you trigger your tinkertech, the dice are rolled on whether it works or fails. The more versatile and powerful the tinkertech is, the greater the chance of failure and the slimmer the chance of success. Depending on the tinkertech and how it functions, this gamble may only apply for its initial activation or each individual use, with the odds adjusted accordingly.

A second handicap is that the more potent the tinkertech you create, the greater the danger and odds of it backfiring if it fails. Consequences can range from simply not working or safely shutting down to catastrophic disasters, such as the parahuman clone you just made trying to kill you. You can adjust these odds, building safer tinkertech at the cost of it having a far lower chance to activate successfully or vice versa.

For example, a ray gun with a 1-in-6 chance of successfully shooting on each trigger pull could take down a mid-level Brute. In contrast, an orbital cannon with a 1-in-100 chance of firing (and a notable chance of catastrophic failure) could kill an Endbringer. You have an innate awareness of the chances and risks involved with your tech.

title: (Tinker) Material Density
description_plain:
You are capable of building advanced technology that manipulates density to compress materials into hyperdense states. Unlike other examples of density manipulation you might know about, this technology operates by reducing the space between different atoms and the arrangement of subatomic particles. As an example, you could fit a hundred tons of steel into a one-inch cube using a special industrial process.

Hyperdense materials are useful for more than an ease of storage as they tend to be exceptionally durable, and if the matter is arranged correctly, it can start displaying various useful properties—like say, a sphere of hyperdense iron being the perfect centerpiece for an electromagnetic shield generator or hyperdense silver being critical to the development of a handheld railgun.

You can’t make something so dense that it becomes a black hole. You can, however, make various types of neutronium with various applications once you’ve fully built up this tech tree.

It is probably possible to apply this technology to organic life without destroying that life, such as with a decent bit of tech development or synergy with other Tinker powers. But by itself, the goal of this power in particular is to fit hundreds of tons of material into personal equipment you can hit people with, shoot people with, or defend yourself with.

As an example—power armor that has simple or even basic functions as far as other Tinkers are concerned, but has more mass than most buildings, providing the wearer immense durability and strength.

title: (Tinker) AI Generated
description_plain:
You are technically a Tinker with a decently versatile knowledge base, but the way your power is formatted you'll struggle to create anything yourself. This is because the knowledge you possess hardly contains any schematics or the instincts to create completely new technology.

One of the only things this power provides you the schematics and instincts to create is 3D printers with integrated AI.

The AI iterates on all technological knowledge it is programmed with. You can give it a prompt for a piece of Tinkertech, and it will do its best to create it in the 3D printer.

The designs for this Tinkertech can either be randomly generated by the AI or a recreation of an already known design, such as a design the AI previously generated.

Technology created through random generation will often need to be modified to get rid of bugs or faults in the design. For example, you might get power armor with only four fingers on a hand, or a cure for the common cold that makes your skin blue.

Your techbase and the quality of Tinkertech your AI powered 3d printers can put together is generally comparable to (Tinker) Basic Tinker.

title: (Tinker) Stasis
description_plain:
You possess a specialty in freezing objects in both space and time. Your technology generally revolves around one scientific mechanism that allows you to freeze objects relative to the nearest major gravity well, which will typically be Earth. Frozen objects are invulnerable and stationary, able to take arbitrary amounts of force without deforming or moving.

You can create guns that can shoot blasts that freeze objects, for between 15 seconds to 5 minutes, though with work and good materials you could compress or shift this range. You can create bombs, generators, or boxes that temporarily or permanently freeze all space within a radius or area.

This power also gives you a relatively simple way to freeze small objects permanently. This allows a variety of different feats of construction, from space elevators to indestructible bunkers to floating skybases. The energy cost of freezing an object this way rises more than linearly with its volume, so applying the method to brick sized objects and building with those tends to be the best option.

What you can freeze, you can also figure out how to unfreeze, though it is a bit harder. Your knowledge in this regard may be applicable to other powers; you could likely figure out how to pop Grayboy bubbles, though doing so safely would be tricky (there's a reason those haven't been popped yet).

At the highest end of your tech tree, with a lot of effort and perhaps investigating other space related tinkertech/powers, you might even be able to change the reference frame of the objects you freeze, allowing you to shoot unstoppable projectiles.

Frozen objects are invulnerable and stationary, able to take arbitrary amounts of force without deforming or moving.

You can create guns that can shoot blasts that freeze objects, for between 15 seconds to 5 minutes, though with work and good materials you could compress or shift this range. You can create bombs, generators, or boxes that temporarily or permanently freeze all space within a radius or area.

This power also gives you a relatively simple way to freeze small objects permanently. This allows a variety of different feats of construction, from space elevators to indestructible bunkers to floating skybases. The energy cost of freezing an object this way rises more than linearly with its volume, so applying the method to brick sized objects and building with those tends to be the best option.

What you can freeze, you can also figure out how to unfreeze, though it is a bit harder. Your knowledge in this regard may be applicable to other powers; you could likely figure out how to pop Grayboy bubbles, though doing so safely would be tricky (there's a reason those haven't been popped yet).

At the highest end of your tech tree, with a lot of effort and perhaps investigating other space related tinkertech/powers, you might even be able to change the reference frame of the objects you freeze, allowing you to shoot unstoppable projectiles.

title: (Tinker) Metropolis
description_plain:
You are a Tinker focused on architecture and urbanism. You can construct buildings and cities, small or massive, though this specialization is very hungry for space, materials and labor.

You can design and build buildings of any scale, from shacks, villas, bunkers, skyscrapers, to megabuildings. You gain a variety of tech for use specifically in architecture, such as load-bearing antigrav generating girders, self-healing walls and inner structure, reconfigurable modular prefab rooms, digitized space that can make the inner floor plan up to twice as large.

Beyond individual buildings, you also gain specialization in the civic infrastructure to run entire communities, from small communes, villages, suburbs, major towns to megacities. This includes decentralized automated utility and service stations, webs of subterranean logistics and hyperspeed transit railways, spatially optimized roads and walking paths that perfect the flow of traffic, and municipal AI that can adapt to any emergency or shift in needs.

This pairs well with (Tinker) Construction and (Tinker) Materials, and could put you just short of creating a plan to turn Earth into an ecumenopolis, though it won’t help you get over all of the many non-material obstacles to that.

title: (Tinker/Thinker) Suppress, Conjecture, Predict
description_plain:
You are a Tinker with a very focused and narrow function: to contain, isolate, and maintain any entity, phenomenon, or anomaly for study. You can design facilities where each block and every cell is a containment zone, capable of stopping or at least slowing down what is inside. Naturally, the entire facility itself acts as a containment zone as well.

You can design esoteric methods of containment, such as time-stopped cells, multi-dimensional closed spaces, and the use of non-euclidean matter-energy. You also ensure that these containment methods keep occupants functional, alive, and isolated from the environment, while still allowing them to be studied by others.

You have an innate understanding of potential escape methods, allowing you to create custom-designed cells that are escape-proof for their intended occupants. However, these cells are less efficient if used to contain anything other than what they were specifically designed for.

title: (Tinker) Rube Goldberg Machines
description_plain:
You are a Tinker capable of touching most specialties and tech trees to one degree or another, specializing in the construction of Rube Goldberg Machines, or rather, chain reactions designed to perform tasks in an indirect and overly complicated way. On average, this often manifests as making dozens of small-scale devices that individually have limited capabilities but interact and activate in a chain reaction to perform tasks of significance.

The longer a chain, the more potent the result, as the devices amplify and modify the chain reaction. For example, an air gun part of a dozen-device-long chain could send a grown Lung flying miles. Chain reactions can be interrupted, which produces less impressive but chaotic and unpredictable results, depending on how far along the chain reaction is.

It usually helps performance if there is distance between all devices when they activate.

After a few dozen devices are added to a chain you start getting diminishing returns on the amplification of the chain reaction, and by a hundred the only thing further devices add is a method of transporting the result of the chain reaction, though you could probably blow a hole through an Endbringer if you land a solid hit with such a chain.

This power perfectly synergizes with any other Tinker power so long as its theme is followed.

description_plain:

You can even design brain-to-machine devices that can implant skills onto people or copy skills from VR simulations to train soldiers for war, making them veterans before they even step onto the battlefield.

You can also enhance classroom experiences by creating augmented reality tech to develop unique learning environments.

You could go into an underperforming school, identify all its flaws—from how it functions to how the teachers teach—and fix every potential problem. You could even train people to become better teachers, creating a virtuous cycle.

title: (Tinker/Thinker) Safety
description_plain:
You can create technology that can keep people safe from all sorts of harm. Your inventions are able to provide a variety of defense mechanisms, including force fields, bunkers, and more. This not only allows you to protect people from physical threats but also to keep them safe from the dangers of the environment.

Moreover, you have the potential to enhance tinkertech, making it safer to use. You can create devices that are less prone to malfunctions. Additionally, you can also scale down certain technology to keep it from causing damage to its user.

As you explore different areas, you gain the ability to sense the safety of your surroundings. You can immediately detect any potential hazards and identify how safe or dangerous an area is. This comes with a wealth of knowledge of various safety techniques, allowing you to recognize common safety hazards and how to avoid them. For example, you can spot a defective power plug and know how to safely deactivate it to prevent electrocution. Similarly, if you come across a construction site, you can quickly identify any violations of safety regulations and advise the workers to fix any issues before continuing.

title: (Tinker) Remote Control
description_plain:
You are a Tinker specializing in remote-controlled technology such as drones. The average Drone built with average resources when starting is initially very limited, maybe comparable to rats, but can swarm in numbers limited only by computer management and communication technology.

Drones can be improved with research and development. They can be given specialized roles and technologies for different purposes, but that is initially limited to things like a taser drone or a flame lighter drone. Other facets of this specialty besides drones and the associated support technology are various bits and pieces that allow advanced communication between technology, advanced computers, advanced programming (not capable of making advanced AI by itself without years of development), and computer-brain interface technology.

title: (Tinker/Striker) Fuinjutsu
description_plain:
You have an interesting Tinker specialty, as it gives you three focuses. First, special inks are made with various materials. Second, symbols are made to be written or drawn with the earlier ink. Lastly, papers are made to have the earlier symbols drawn on them. All together, they form Seals.

The inks, depending on what material is used to make them, will have different properties, from fire-like properties or gravity-based properties. The symbols are used to channel the properties, specifying what they are to do. The paper is its output; the better the paper, the stronger and/or more stable the effect. To put it in perspective, the ink is the type of programming language, the symbols are the code itself, and the paper is the hardware.

When you activate the Seal, the paper will stick to whatever it was placed on, applying its effect to it. A minor effect you also gain is an increased skill in handwriting and brushwork.

title: (Tinker) Huge Scale
description_plain:
This Tinker specialty could be considered a conceptual mirror of Colin Wallis’s power. Instead of technology focused on efficiency and miniaturization, this power focuses its techbase on increasing the size and effective capabilities of its technology. To put it simply, you specialize in Effectiveness and Magnification.

Essentially, the bigger you design a piece of technology, the more ideas you get for increasing the effectiveness and power of its functions. You’ll also have an easier time designing things to be durable and survive various environments the bigger you make them.

So this specialty truly shines in the construction of large structures such as building-sized robots, fortresses, battleships, or even outrageously huge energy cannons. Say you build a mecha as large as an Endbringer; with sufficient skill and a bit of luck, you just might be able to singlehandedly drive off an Endbringer just as a hypothetical alternate universe Colin could with his armor, prediction system, and nanothorn.

Just like Colin, you have a versatile and wide-ranging techbase covering most forms of Tinkertech.

title: (Tinker) Satellites
description_plain:
You specialise in the design, construction, launch and operation of artificial satellites and similar orbital spacecraft.

Your satellites can serve an enormous variety of purposes, whether intended for communication, surveillance, navigation, defence, habitation or other applications. They may be deployed across a wide range of trajectories and altitudes, from a low earth orbit of 500 km up to a geostationary orbit of over 35,000 km away.

You could build a world-wide broadcasting network, telescopes that can map countries and monitor individuals from space, weather forecasting systems accurate weeks in advance, habitable spacecraft or platforms equipped with powerful laser weaponry. For example, you might deploy observation satellites to track parahuman activity or, with sufficient effort, create a planetary orbital defense array.

This pairs well with numerous other Tinker specialities; for example, if combined with Lookout, you could build the perfect spy satellites, or, with Mannequin, an expansive, self-sustaining space station.

title: (Tinker) Escalation
description_plain:
Your Tinker specialty is creating tinkertech that enhances itself through combat. By engaging in combat, your tech will start to ‘mature’, gaining features that make it stronger, better, and more versatile as time passes. By default, the maturing process takes 30 minutes; however, this scales in proportion to the scale and danger of the combat. Should you leave combat or combat end before the current maturing process is done, the tech will slowly start to revert to its original state. The process can be rekindled should combat start again.

When the maturing process finishes, another will start up soon after if the user is still in combat. Additions to your tech that have finished maturing can be added onto other tech like normal tinkertech.

title: (Tinker) Assimilation
description_plain:
You are a minor Free Tinker whose specialty revolves around the concept of Assimilation. Essentially, you can create various types of basic tinkertech from most tech trees available.

However, this technology will, by default, always include some way to meld with other objects to increase its capabilities as part of its design. Fighting this aspect and excluding those elements from a design will drastically lower your technology's capabilities, if it even functions at all.

Examples of how your technology melds with other objects could include a nanite swarm, adaptive mutagenic retroviruses, or even a specialized computer virus. It all depends on what it’s trying to meld with and how you designed it to meld in the first place, as a computer program probably isn’t going to be able to meld with anything physically unless it also contains some sort of physical element to it.

You can put in parameters for how and what your technology can meld with when you design it. Particularly strong immune systems and other defenses can prevent your technology from melding with other objects, especially if the example of your tech in question isn’t particularly advanced, powerful, or is damaged in some capacity.

This specialty includes ways to modify your technology after it melds with new objects to make sure it develops along paths you desire. You can also design your technology with certain capabilities that only activate once it acquires enough mass from melding, such as mitosis-style replication or self-repair.

title: (Tinker) Probability Manipulation
description_plain:
You specialize in constructing technology that manipulates probability fields, subtly stacking the deck in your favor. Your devices don't create impossibilities; they stack the odds until the improbable becomes nearly inevitable, though absolute certainty is always out of reach. No matter how much energy or processing power you commit, you cannot force an outcome to 100% or reduce another to 0%. The more you push an event closer to certainty, the more energy and computational power it consumes, making total guarantees impossible.

The complexity of the task is your primary constraint. Influencing a simple event, like a coin toss, is trivial. However, complex chains of events, such as causing a sniper's bullet to ricochet off three surfaces to hit a target, require immense processing power and energy. After enacting such a change, your equipment must recalibrate, as the "butterfly effect" of your action throws all previously calculated variables into chaos, effectively putting the device on a cooldown.

Your influence is limited by time and range. The power works best on a scale of minutes and is ineffective beyond a day. Handheld devices operate within fifty feet, while larger emplacements with dedicated power sources can influence probabilities across the city. Pushing an event farther from its natural probability costs exponentially more energy and processing power, as well as increasing the risk of unintended consequences.

This specialization pairs especially well with (Tinker) Detection and Analysis, (Tinker) Kinesis, and (Tinker) Quantum Computing.

title: (Tinker/Master) Machine World
description_plain:
You can transform into and manifest materials to create machines you understand or tinkertech specialties that you have out of your own body. While this harms you, you also have a minor regeneration power to keep you alive.

You will have a link that enables you to control any machine that is made from you within 1 km, although you can make relays to extend this range as well as fuse with them as long as they are in touching range. This doesn’t come with multitasking abilities.

This synergizes well with other tinker powers. Note that without some kind of regeneration power, this can be extremely risky.

Examples of uses for this power are making metal spikes extrude from your skin for combat or vomiting molten metal to forge. More advanced uses include creating entire machines, such as robots (either from understanding their materials, systems, and mechanics or from a tinker specialty), directly rather than just creating the materials, but doing this is harder, riskier, and even more painful.

title: (Tinker) Nanites
description_plain:
This power grants you a Tinker specialty revolving around nanotechnology. Nano-scale technology has a variety of purposes, but to list a few examples, you could make nanites for construction, spying, and even flying destructive swarms.

But you aren’t limited to just swarms of nanites; you may also construct larger pieces of generic Tinkertech out of nanites, such as armor, weaponry, and cybernetics. The nanites coming together to take the shape and functions of various electronic and mechanical components.

Though versatile, the larger pieces of Tinkertech you can construct out of nanites can only be considered average compared to the casual work of a dedicated specialty.

By necessity, given the limited space within a nanite for technological functions, different types of nanites will possess and specialize in different functions. A few examples could be one type of nanite focusing on delivering energy to other nanites, another might focus on serving as a signal relay, and a third type might focus on serving as the structure of any larger pieces of Tinkertech you might construct out of nanites.

Your nanites can be programmed to take on different shapes in different situations or in response to different signals. Like a suit of nanite power armor that can take the shape of clothing when in a casual setting, just by taking advantage of the fact that nanites are objects measured in nanometers, allowing vast quantities of nanites to fit in small configurations for easy storage when not in use.

Though when taking on smaller configurations, your nanites will not possess the capabilities of any larger pieces of technology they can form. So that aforementioned suit of nanite power armor, when in the form of clothing, they won’t have the protective qualities, strength augmenting servos, and other technological functions of power armor.

One final thing to note is that, despite specializing in nanotechnology, this power does not include any designs or instincts for creating a grey goo nanite apocalypse. Though synergy with other powers could let you bypass this limitation.

title: (Tinker) Lasers!
description_plain:
This power is to Legend’s Shard what Hero’s is to Stilling. You have the capacity to make devices that produce lasers with various effects, limited by your creativity and the research you do.

Examples include lasers that can turn corners, fork into multiple lasers, pass through walls, freeze, ignite targets, cut, disintegrate, impact, heat, focus, staccato bursts, fat lasers, and invisible lasers. These are just examples, though you could develop lasers with capabilities other than those examples and combine effects. Your power also isn't limited to just these forms of esoteric energy manipulation and support technology; the true purpose for this power is space travel, so beyond dealing with harmful space energies, a form of FTL technology might not be out of reach, especially if this power is whiteboxed.

title: (Tinker) Information
description_plain:
You can create machines capable of manipulating raw information. In its most basic state, you can create Stranger effects, such as making specific information impossible to process, causing it to slip from memory. You can also create machines meant to analyze others to gain information. In its more advanced stages, you could transform the state of information, converting virtual data into physical form and vice versa. The only flaw is that your technology has a limited range, incapable of affecting those far away.

This pairs extremely well with (Tinker) Meme and (Tinker) Informational Hazard.

title: (Tinker) Infectious Enhancements
description_plain:
You specialize in the construction of all manner of cybernetic and biological modifications. Though versatile such enhancements are, at their best, only mildly above average compared to the casual work of a dedicated Tinker specialty. But that’s only when you compare the aspects this power shares with other enhancement focused Tinker specialties.

The unique area where this power shines is that you can design every enhancement you make to be infectious.

For example, say you enhanced someone with wolf based cybernetics and bio modifications, that person could bite other people injecting them with a mix of nanites and mutagen which would slowly but surely modify their body to possess similar enhancements.

These infections take resources from the host body to build the desired cybernetics or biological modifications.

It takes on average a month for someone infected by your Tinkertech to be fully enhanced by an average example of your work. Though that timescale can be sped up or lengthened depending on the complexity of the enhancements in question and how completely they alter the host body. Though obviously that only applies to people being infected by sources of your Tinkertech instead of someone you directly modify.

Depending on the enhancements being made, an infected individual might experience an increased appetite. That hunger comes from their infection driving them to gather the materials it needs to make its enhancements. The things they can be driven to be hungry for can include inorganic material such gold, uranium, or platinum depending on the enhancements being made. Not consuming such materials can slow or even halt the infection progress depending on why that material was needed in the first place.

Your Tinkertech enhancements can be designed to be capable of self repair, drawing resources from the host body to repair damage and preform maintenance at a rate similar to a normal human's healing factor.

You can design your Tinkertech enhancements to possess multiple strains of enhancements they can infect people with. As an example, say you enhance someone with cybernetics and bio modifications based on vampire characteristics. This artificial vampire could produce two strains; the first is obviously more vampires, while the second could be a ghoul strain that has most of the same capabilities as the vampire strain just weakened and innately loyal to vampires.

As for what determines what strain manifests it could be as simple as the person doing the infection choosing or a response to different conditions you programmed it to respond to.

Unless they are specifically made to be compatible or don’t interfere with each other people can’t be infected by multiple strains of your enhancements. They can however be infected with new strains that’ll replace their previous enhancements. This requires either a successful handshake protocol between strains or for the new strain to be able to ignore the defenses of the previous strain.

Your infections aren’t absolute, things like sufficiently enhanced immune systems, specific forms of Parahuman healing, and the work of other Tinkers can prevent or cure an infection.

title: (Tinker) Souls Tech
description_plain:
Have you ever heard of “Soulslike”? It’s a particularly difficult genre of action RPG. Why is that relevant? Well, the technology this power provides you seems particularly focused on replicating a similar style of combat and risk in you with a sci-fi twist.

First and foremost, you can create a network of machines that have many different functions that will be touched upon throughout the rest of this power’s description. These machines are also individually rather small, about the size of the average bonfire. So, for the sake of simplicity, these machines will be called bonfires throughout the rest of this power’s description.

Several basic applications for these bonfires include: reviving you in the event of your death, teleportation between different bonfires, healing you, and providing maintenance for your other pieces of Tinkertech equipment.

Your bonfires can also shift out of phase with normal reality, becoming intangible and invisible to avoid danger, an effect they can extend to when you’re making use of a bonfire. Though you won’t be able to affect the outside universe until the effect ends.

When you first start with this power, you’ll also be able to build basic Tinkertech cybernetics, bio augmentations, weapons, and armor. Along with a basic Tinkertech pocket dimensions to store and retrieve materials and equipment from.

Know that in the event of your death that when a bonfire revives you, you’ll revive with all of the equipment you had on your person before death, including any cybernetics and bioaugmentations you added to your body.

The way your bonfires revive you and repair your other Tinkertech is rather unique, in that it involves space-time manipulation to retrieve your body and equipment while making all repairs necessary to make it as if you never died and your Tinkertech was never damaged.

Unless you set it up to work otherwise, in the event of your death, you’ll revive at the last bonfire you interacted with.

Another function of this power is the ability to gather data from combat, using Tinkertech cameras and sensors that can be made into cybernetics.

You can use that data to slowly but surely improve the designs for your non-bonfire Tinkertech until you reach the pinnacle of Parahuman power.

It should be noted that different combat encounters give different quality data; so, a hundred combat encounters with mundane crooks might give you the data needed to improve a particular type of basic Tinkertech you used by a few percent; meanwhile, a prolonged combat encounter against a Parahuman could give you the data needed to improve your equipment by dozens of percentages.

Data you gather from combating Parahumans and other foes beyond the mundane can also be used to make equipment that can partially replicate their capabilities in some capacity. Say a battle with Lung might give you the data needed to make a greatsword that can light itself on fire, and can tune the energy it gives off to slowly get better at burning a target the longer it's used in combat against them.

One final thing to note is that you can use your bonfires as a basic general-purpose Tinker workshop, allowing you to make basic modifications to your Tinkertech while out on the field away from more substantial workshops.

title: (Tinker) Terraforming
description_plain:
You are a tinker specializing in environmental technology with dual approaches to that specialty. One approach focuses on surviving hostile environments in various ways, from specialized genemods, cybernetics, armor/clothing, vehicles, or shelters. The other focuses on changing the environment to suit your needs, like purifying water on a large scale, changing the composition of the gases in the air, manipulating the materials composing the ground, dealing with radiation, dealing with heat or a lack of heat, and changing the weather.

These approaches are not incompatible; if you work at it, you might be able to make cybernetics or armor that can shoot bolts of electricity or manipulate the environment in various ways.

While this specialty is very versatile, it does not surpass specialties like (Tinker) Thermal or (Tinker) Cybernetics in their field, as it merely offers a specialized approach. It has great synergy with specialties related to either of its approaches.

description_plain:
You can create pieces of technology that can either amplify or dampen parahuman powers. The limits on how much you can diminish/boost powers depend on the tinkertech’s size and your experience in your power’s usage and practice; the smaller your tech is, the smaller the range, to the point where rings or necklace-sized pieces of technology require physical contact to work, but in exchange for this limitation, the smaller the piece of technology, the more powerful the amplification/dampening is, with the boosting/dampening’s maximum limit being 1000% of the original power. At first, you will barely be able to create pieces of tinkertech that can boost or dampen parahuman powers by 10% and are roughly the same size as a portable gas generator.

And if you have Negentropy, then your technology becomes geared to recharge and supercharge Shards. Along with this, the boost your technology gives can reach over 1000%.

title: (Tinker/Trump) Variable Tinker
description_plain:
When you trigger this power, you get a single, somewhat random, Tinker specialization centred around solving a problem of your choice. This Tinker specialization can only be on par with a Tier 1 Tinker power at most, but it's generally oriented around helping you with whatever problem you present to it.

This specialization can stay for either a maximum of 1 month or as long as the problem persists, whichever is shorter. You can freely drop your Tinker specialization and acquire a new one at any time. You have an instinctive understanding of what your Tinker specialization is and have full access to the Tinker technology tree encompassed by it, akin to a normal Tinker.

You can operate and maintain any tinkertech you've previously built, regardless of your current specialization, but you cannot build it from scratch again. You may also integrate and mix tinkertech from your current specialization into previously constructed tinkertech, but you're unable to do the reverse.

title: (Tinker) Living Metallurgist
description_plain:
You are a Tinker who specializes in the construction of living metals, a multitude of different metallic substances that possess DNA and various other organic properties.

These organic properties include but are not limited to: living metal being able to passively self-repair and maintain itself if it has adequate access to energy and resources while not damaged beyond repair. You’ll also find that, similar to different organic organisms, different types of living metal excel in different environments like the desert, rainforest, Mars, Antarctica, or even the deep sea.

You will find it easy to recycle or modify Tinkertech made out of living metal, using forms of genetic manipulation technology provided by this power that specializes in the manipulation of living metal DNA.

Another big benefit to living metal is the way it communicates with itself, saving space in the Tinkertech you construct. Essentially, technology made of living metal has little need for cables and other such methods to transmit instructions to its various components.

This is because living metal, in addition to its other capabilities, can be used as a medium to transmit information and instruments to other pieces of living metal and technology if it is physically connected to either, all while being used to form the frame, armor, or even the entirety of a piece of Tinkertech.

This specialty is capable of touching most forms of Tinkertech constructed out of inorganic materials to one degree or another, such as melee weapons, guns, armor, computers, circuitry, cybernetics, or robots—just to name a few examples.

While this specialty is versatile, it does not surpass specialties like (Tinker) Robots or (Tinker) Cybernetics in their field, as it merely offers a specialized approach. It has great synergy with specialties that focus on the construction of tinkertech out of inorganic materials, especially metals.

title: (Tinker) Fastest Tinker Alive
description_plain:
You have access to an extremely basic, low-end database of generic tinkertech. To say you got the short end of the stick, to have 'lost’ the Tinker lottery is… a lie. Because you have something all those other Tinkers don't have enough of: Time. Not in the sense that you can give yourself more of it, or something to that effect. But rather, you have more time in the sense that you tinker so impossibly fast that you make use of the time you have far better than any other Tinker ever could.

You tinker approximately 25x faster compared to the average Tinker, without sacrificing even a shred of quality from your creations. The sponge that takes much of a Tinker’s time, that of maintaining all of their creations, becomes a mere fraction of your day rather than a fair chunk of it. This allows you to maintain even more pieces of tinkertech than a Tinker reasonably could.

Furthermore, this allows you the option to adopt a reckless 'playstyle’ that would normally be dashed away as inefficient by the rest of the world: Tinkering in the middle of combat, and in environments that are not prepared by the Tinker in advance. Having a small army of expendable drones hold off your enemy as you use the surrounding materials to give yourself additional means of fighting your opponents is now a viable strategy for you to perform.

You still require materials like any other Tinker, and this doesn't negate the weakness of time entirely, merely allowing you to do far more with what time you have.

title: (Blaster) Debuff
description_plain: You can modify your projectiles to apply a debuff, such as burn, stun, caustic, poisonous, disease, hypnotic, sensory deprivation, or fatigue.

title: (Blaster) David’s Sling
description_plain:
The microsecond you launch a projectile, whether via a weapon, your hands or any other means, you can instantaneously accelerate it up to the muzzle velocity of a standard M16 rifle round, approximately 960 m/s.

For example, a thrown penny would carry similar kinetic energy to that of a handgun’s bullet whereas a brick could strike with force equivalent to an autocannon shell. You can set the exact speed of your projectiles, which follow normal aerodynamics after acceleration.

title: (Blaster) Handcannon
description_plain: You can shoot blasts out from your hands that hit with the force of a sledgehammer, and move at roughly 100km/h. These blasts can be modified, such as increasing the blast angle in exchange for effective range, thinning them to increase their piercing power, lowering their force to increase their speed, or lowering their overall power for sustained fire. You cannot have more than one modification happening at a time.

title: (Blaster) Hand Lights
description_plain: You can create beams of energy that can connect and interact with the real world instead of destroying it. You can control how thin these get and how large they get. While there is no range, you cannot sense through them.

title: (Blaster/Thinker) Stop-Hit
description_plain:
Any projectile utilized by you - thrown, fired, etcetera - immediately reaches the endpoint of its trajectory, connecting in an instant. Stones flung from slings disappear into thin air, reappearing right in front of an enemy’s head. Bullets exit the barrel and simply pop back into reality a millimeter away from contact. Your power takes the beginning and end of the trajectory, and cuts out the time between the two.

The ‘ghost trajectory’ of your projectiles, by default, ignores nearly every environmental factor present that could affect its direction. Like an FPS character, anywhere you point a gun is where the bullet will land. No wind affecting where it goes, no gravity dragging it downwards. However, its effective range remains the same - neither friction nor air resistance can be ignored, as do other such relevant forces, unless they’re actively shortening the projectile’s natural effective range. Alternatively, you could choose to let select factors affect the ghost trajectory individually, allowing you to plan your shots much more effectively. If bullet drop can help you land a good shot, you can let gravity affect the trajectory.

This means you can teleport anything you throw for as far as you can throw it, as well. To assist your control over this power, you gain an understanding of your ghost trajectory as it moves according to the objects you plan to throw, and as it shifts depending on what environmental factors you choose to exclude from it.

title: (Blaster/Master) Skill Thief
description_plain:
You can absorb the practical expertise of anyone you focus on.

The skills you can absorb can be increased by things such as eye contact or physical contact, with each connection made increasing the breadth and depth of what you are able to steal, whether a specific skill or a target's general skill set.

Unless you completely steal a target's skill, they will regain the skill over time.

You permanently retain any stolen skills and can improve them by re-stealing partially stolen skills or stealing similar skills.

title: (Blaster) Mutation
description_plain: You gain a short-ranged Blaster power, taking the form of writhing, near-invisible "whips" of energy. These whips are Manton limited, allowing them to pass through inorganic matter only. The whips work by inducing debilitating, permanent physical mutations on those struck. Examples include: having the targets legs fused into a single mangled, paralysed limb or having heavy tangle of bone snakes grow between the targets ribcage making every breath a struggle.

title: (Blaster) Shibari
description_plain:
You can conjure and launch tangled orbs of forcefield bindings. These orbs will uncurl and tangle around whatever it hits, binding the object in the most immobilizing way possible.

If an orb strikes an already entangled object, its energy will be absorbed into the existing bindings, making them stronger, tighter and thinner, digging into and slicing the object.

The entanglements will dissipate if it takes significant damage, or if the object its surrounding is destroyed.

title: (Blaster/Striker) First Strike
description_plain:
You are always the first to strike, no matter the situation. Even if an opponent tries to attack you first, your attack will land before theirs. Your body reacts automatically, and reality subtly bends to ensure your attack connects first.

This works at any range. Whether someone fires at you from another city or charges you at superhuman speed, your strike will always reach them before their attack hits you.

title: (Blaster) Bloodlet
description_plain:

description_plain:

These crystals, when broken, violently “explode”, directly applying varying amounts of heat and outward force to anything nearby based on how close it was to the crystal and how large the crystal itself was, with crystals the size of a pebble equalling a strong grenade. The absolute nature of this explosion means it ignores the protective capabilities of any armour.

You have telekinetic control over these crystals and can break them at will. You also have a vague understanding of the location of these crystals relative to yourself.

description_plain:

Whether you know their name, their personality, their fears, or even a single detail about their past, each bit of knowledge enhances the potency of your actions.

This power isn’t limited to dealing damage; it affects any interaction you have with your target. If you choose to harm or torment, even the smallest fact, like a nickname or a habit, will magnify their suffering, bringing their deepest vulnerabilities to the surface.
